text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Minister of Transport Alexander Rezes said Slovakia planned to invest around 300 billion crowns to develop road and telecommunication networks. Most of the funds should go for motorway construction.
- Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) has strongly rejected media reports about Meciar's alleged serious illness.

- The state river transport company SPD has rejected allegations that the crash of a Slovak boat at the unfinished Freudenau power plant near Vienna was caused either by the technical state of the boat, or a captain's error.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Slovakia's largest savings bank, state-run Slovenska Sporitelna, has called an extraordinary shareholders meeting for November 11. Changes to the company's supervisory board are the only item on the agenda.

- The volume of loans provided by Slovak banks and the National Bank of Slovakia rose by 6.3 billion crowns in August, increasing the total volume to 353.7 billion crowns. Banks extended loans worth 314.4 billion in crowns, with the remaining 39.3 billion extended in foreign currencies.
- The first block of Slovakia's second nuclear power plant Mochovce is expected to start operation in 1998, as originally planned.
- Steel producer VSZ is seriously interested in building a water pipeline system in Montenegro.
SME - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik is expected to be replaced by the director of Devin Banka, Karol Martinka. Kozlik should remain a deputy prime minister for economy.

PRAVDA - Julius Toth, head of the state-run engineering industry coordinator DMD Holding, said the company plans to increase production to 29 billion crowns from the current four billion over the next three years. Arms production is planned to account for 15 percent, Toth said.
